correctness.rationale: D commutes with normalized convolution. A Jordan coupling of mass V(f)/2 bounds amplification by half the maximum L1 distance of two normalized translates; opposite point masses from an arc attain each nonzero tested distance. For h=delta/2 and c=cos(h), the centered unnormalized difference is -4 sin(h) sin(u)(1+4c cos(u)), whose absolute integral on the two half-periods gives exactly the two branches in (2). The first reaches at most 4/pi. On the second, the derivative of the squared ratio times 4 pi^2 has sign given by -(16z+1)(32z^2-16z+1), with z=c^2, and the only interior maximum has z=(2+sqrt(2))/8 and value 71+8sqrt(2), larger than 64. Both boundary cases are smaller. Reflection gives only the two complementary lengths. The radical decimals agree. No all-BV equality classification is implied.
residual_risks: Real scalar field and exact quotient by constants are essential to the argument; no claim about complex BV or arbitrary cutoff follows.
